method: Read630 additional keyboard/clipboard operation lines. Ran exact timestamp predicates against owned synthetic SQLite data; no upstream UI execution.
findings: Pin/delete/edit operations use timestamp extracted from clip presentation id rather than clipboard_history primary id. Earlier writer records millisecond timestamps without uniqueness check. Synthetic two-row same-timestamp fixture: exact UPDATE predicate pinned2 rows and DELETE predicate removed2, while different-timestamp control survived. Does not measure actual collision rate or execute upstream application.

Clipboard edit/copy SELECT by timestamp uses query_row without deterministic tie selection; when timestamps collide, selecting one displayed record can read a different matching row. Same timestamp also underlies selection normalization and visual IDs, so identity conflation occurs before SQL.

Pin UI updates optimistically before database success and treats execute.is_ok as changed even for0 rows; write failure has no rollback shown. Delete removes displayed results before detached database outcome. No integrated persistence-failure fixture run.

Both Enter-confirm and second-Delete paths issue history DELETE, not file removal. Saved image content paths are not deleted in reviewed branch; lifecycle elsewhere remains unread. No image-file deletion performed.
Delete confirmation requires explicit second Delete or Enter and Escape clears selection/confirmation; review must not characterize this branch as unconditional immediate deletion.

Clipboard edit copies proposed new content even if asynchronous SQL update fails, then closes edit state and refreshes. Unique-content conflicts can therefore leave database old while clipboard holds new; source-level finding, constraint fixture not run.
Form key handler calls handle_form_enter; persistence implementation is outside current read range. This batch does not qualify note/snippet creation save behavior.

Multi-selection copy sorts unique timestamps ascending; HashSet click order is not preserved. Images in mixed copy become textual image paths rather than image payload. This is explicit source behavior, not file-content grouping.
limits: 85/268 whole files; main.rs partial ranges only.
Synthetic SQLite predicate control, not complete upstream schema/Windows integration; no production edits.

executed_controls.fixture: Owned in-memory SQLite, two distinct contents sharing one millisecond timestamp plus different-timestamp control
executed_controls.scope: Exact reviewed WHERE timestamp SQL predicate mechanism; not upstream Windows application or actual event collision frequency.

WHERE timestamp = ?; DELETE FROM clipboard_history WHERE timestamp = ?; assert changed2/deleted2/control survives.
